transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm glad you're here. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... for the last few weeks, I’ve barely had an appetite. It's weird. Usually, after a long shift, I'll get something I normally like to eat, but lately the food just sits there in front of me. I end up just having to force down a few bites. It's just... yeah, that's really what brought me in today.
Over these past few weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling down, sad, or like you've lost interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I feel like I’m carrying around this... heavy, flat feeling. It's like, even when I’m home with my family, or just sitting in the break room on shift, I’m just not really there.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss over these past few weeks?

Yeah, I think so. Like I was saying earlier, for the last few weeks I just haven't had much of an appetite at all. Since I'm really just forcing down a few bites instead of eating my normal meals after work, the weight has definitely been coming off without me trying to lose it.
Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain along with the decreased appetite?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick to my stomach or in any pain. It's really just... I just don't have any desire to eat.
Did these feelings and appetite changes start around the same time as any particular stressful event or change in your life?
Yeah, it actually did. All this has been going on for about three weeks now... it started right around the time the casino reorganized our security operations and changed up my assignments.
Have you noticed any unexplained fevers or night sweats along with the weight loss and low mood?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No fevers... and no night sweats either. My temperature has been totally normal as far as I can tell.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or more sensitive to cold temperatures than usual during these past few weeks?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired, but just the regular kind of tired from not sleeping well and feeling down. But no, I haven't felt unusually cold or anything like that. Just my normal self in that regard.

Besides feeling flat, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, time with friends, or activities outside of work—even when you're not thinking about the job changes?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to my morning runs, and I'd play my guitar a bit, or cook a nice dinner. But lately... I don't know, I just keep skipping all of it. They don't feel enjoyable anymore, they just feel like chores that I can't get myself to care about.
Along with the low mood, have you also been feeling unusually anxious, nervous, or on edge—like you can't stop worrying about the changes at work?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm anxious or on edge. The work stuff is on my mind, sure, but I don't feel nervous about it. It's more just... feeling down and flat, like I said. I'm not really worrying or stressing out, just kind of empty.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless, excessively guilty about things, or any thoughts of harming yourself or that life isn't worth living?

I wouldn't say I feel guilty or worthless, really. But... well, I'm not planning to hurt myself or anything. It's just, I keep having these thoughts lately that maybe it wouldn't be the worst thing if I just didn't wake up. Just so I wouldn't have to keep pushing through all this every day, you know?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 3-week history of depressed/flat mood, marked anhedonia (loss of interest in running, guitar, cooking), significant unintentional weight loss due to poor appetite, fatigue, and passive suicidal ideation (thoughts of not waking up) without active plan or intent. Symptoms occurred nearly every day for most of the day over the 3-week period. Physical causes for weight loss/appetite change (thyroid dysfunction, GI illness, infection) were explicitly ruled out via review of systems (no cold intolerance, no fever/night sweats, no GI symptoms). Although symptoms began temporally with a workplace stressor (reorganization), the clinical picture is dominated by core depressive symptoms (depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight change, suicidal ideation) exceeding what would be expected in a pure adjustment reaction, and anxiety symptoms were explicitly denied, arguing against an anxious adjustment disorder. This meets criteria for a major depressive episode; because this is presented as a single, first episode without stated recurrence, it is coded as unspecified single-episode major depressive disorder (F32.9) pending further history.
